sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. The relevant facts necessary for consideration of the present appeal are that the claimant filed a claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident which occurred on 15.1.2012.

It is the case of the claimant that when he was travelling on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-02/EB 9017 another motor cycle bearing No.KA-04/HB 5308 came and hit his vehicle causing the accident in question.
The owner of the offending vehicle i.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-04/HB 5308 Hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' NC: 2024:KHC:2254 was arrayed as a respondent.
The claimant examined himself as PW.1, the doctor as PW.2 and another witness as PW.3.
Exs. P1
to P21
were marked in evidence.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of the respondent.

4. The Tribunal by its judgment and award dated 6.6.2013 allowed the claim petition and awarded a compensation of `5,48,710/- together with inters at 6% pa., and directed the respondent to pay the compensation awarded.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded.
5. The only question that is to be considered in the present appeal is whether the quantum of compensation is required to be enhanced.
6. It is noticed that only the owner of the vehicle is arrayed as a party to the claim proceedings.
In the above appeal he is served but unrepresented.
7. The age of the claimant has been assessed as 22 years.
Hence, the multiplier assessed by the Tribunal at 18 is NC: 2024:KHC:2254 just and proper.
The claimant has stated that he was working as a driver.
However, since no documentary evidence has been produced, the income of the claimant has been assessed by the Tribunal at `4,000/- pm.

Having regard to the fact that no documents have been produced by the claimant to prove his income, the same is required to be re-assessed as notional income as per the chart followed for settlement of claims in the Lok Adalath conducted by the Legal Service Authority and having regarding regard to the fact that the accident is of the year Sri Yogesh vs Naresh K on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123784079/
2 2012, the income is required to be re-assessed at `7,000/- pm.
8.
The claimant has sustained injuries to the head, fracture of both bones of right leg and mandible fracture.
The claimant has taken treatment as an inpatient for a total period of 84 days in 3 different hospitals.
The doctor - PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability as 10% and the Tribunal has also, upon an appreciation of the evidence on record has assessed the disability at 10%.
9. Having regard to the aforementioned, the quantum of compensation is re
- assessed as follows:

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `15,000/-
towards loss of amenities.
Having regard to the nature of injures sustained and the period of treatment the same is just and proper.
9.2 The Tribunal has assessed a sum of `10,000/- towards conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment.
Having regard to the period of treatment, the same is re-
assessed at `15,000/-.
9.3 The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, the same is re
- assessed at `30,000/-.
9.4 The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `11,200/- towards loss of income during the period of treatment.
The period of treatment is taken as 90 days and the loss of income during the said period is re-
assessed at `21,000/-.
9.5 The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `4,02,910/- towards medical expenses which is just and proper.
9.6 Loss of future earning capacity is re
Accordingly, the total compensation under various heads is re-
assessed as follows:
